topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the scope and conceptual approach of the session on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the fundamental criteria and spatial organization by which the innate immune system detects pathogens and cellular damage through molecular patterns and germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families and signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail specific receptor families, intracellular signaling mechanisms, and inflammasome activation complexes that trigger downstream immune responses upon ligand detection.

topics.label: Inflammatory mediator responses, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the effector processes set off by innate recognition, covering sentinel cell signaling, vascular extravasation, lymphatic priming, and severe systemic manifestations like septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the mechanisms required to terminate inflammation, rebuild damaged tissue, and manage persistent inflammatory states such as fibrosis and granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation and announces the topic of the following lecture.
